withdrawnClaim: That public.corporate_deliverable_command acquires an AccessExclusiveLock on the TABLE public.operation_task_instances, and that this blocks every read and write of operation tasks rather than only corporate ones.
whyItWasWrong: pg_locks.relation is populated for tuple locks as well as relation locks, and the query used to read it did not select locktype. A tuple-level AccessExclusiveLock covers ONE ROW, not the table.

disproof.method: Two ordinary SELECT ... FOR UPDATE transactions against one row of public.operation_task_instances on staging, both rolled back.
disproof.waiterError: ERROR: canceling statement due to lock timeout / CONTEXT: while locking tuple (0,1) in relation "operation_task_instances"
disproof.conclusion: The signature reported as evidence of a table lock is the ordinary signature of row-lock contention. It is produced by lock_operation_authority's SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the task row, which is by design and serialises only commands on the SAME task.

staticCheckSupportingTheWithdrawal: All 20 LOCK TABLE statements across every migration use SHARE mode; there is no bare LOCK TABLE (which would default to ACCESS EXCLUSIVE) anywhere, and every ALTER TABLE / CREATE TRIGGER touching operation_task_instances is migration-time DDL, not runtime.

whatStillHolds.hangIsReal: The request hangs until the client disconnects. The logged duration equals the client timeout every time: 30s browser -> 'POST 200 in 29.6s'; 75s client -> 'POST 200 in 75s'; 40s client -> timeout at 40s. Next logs 200 because no response is ever sent.
whatStillHolds.notPlaywright: A plain urllib POST with a correct Content-Length reproduces it.
whatStillHolds.notTheRevision: A valid expected_revision hangs the same as a bogus one.
whatStillHolds.errorPathHealthy: A malformed payload returns 400 in 0.23s and a 409 appears in the same run.
whatStillHolds.unbounded: Staging has lock_timeout=0 and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=0, so nothing breaks a wait.
whatStillHolds.browserProofFailsOnRestored374: Re-run with 378 applied fails identically, so 376/377 were irrelevant and withdrawing them was correct.

rootCause: STILL NOT IDENTIFIED. Row-lock contention on the task row explains why concurrent commands on one task serialise, but not why a holder never completes. Sequential commands finish in about 1.15s; 88 succeeded in the same run.
nextHypothesisNotEvidence: prepare with source_family=census executes LOCK TABLE public.census_daily_log IN SHARE MODE. SHARE conflicts with ROW EXCLUSIVE, so any concurrent writer to census_daily_log would block it indefinitely given lock_timeout=0. This is an untested hypothesis, recorded to direct the next step, not a finding.
boundaries: No production, provider, email, Front Office receiver, live schedule, staff or operating acceptance was performed or claimed. COL-160 remains incomplete and COL-326 remains open with its cause unestablished.
